old: The verdict rests on two independent sources rather than one sample: the notice observed on eight paths across two domains today, and the parent company's own filed exhibit. Three other explanations for the page were considered and refuted. (1) A WAF or challenge page: refuted, because the response is a 200 carrying a page titled for the FBI and because it is served on /robots.txt, which no vendor challenge covers. (2) A parked or lapsed domain: refuted by that title and by the exhibit naming a seizure on 2026-07-02. (3) An operator-side DNS or origin fault: refuted because all eight paths on both hostnames returned byte-identical responses of 297,312 bytes, which is one served document rather than eight independent failures. What is not settled: whether the domains return, and whether any NetNut endpoint survives on a hostname not tried here. Alarum's update says only that it continued to analyse the incident, so nothing read today establishes restoration. Two deviations are deliberate. The interface list carries 'unknown' because the assignment's vocabulary (api, socks5, http-proxy, web-ui and the rest) is not in scripts/dossier/schema.json, whose enum ends at 'unknown', and no page read here established an interface anyway. The quote supplied with the assignment shortens the exhibit's 'by the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigations ("FBI")' to 'by the FBI'; the evidence entry quotes the exhibit verbatim. This record corrects no other topic's record, because no dossier file anywhere in the tree carried NetNut before it: grep over dossier/ returns this file and nothing else, so the name lived only in scratch under .tmp/ — the ip-proxy lane-6 candidate list that queued https://netnut.io/pricing/, the debrid sweep name lists, and the market-report extracts that still recommend it. That is why third-party comparison tables still carry the vendor, and why this record exists.
new: Alarum Technologies, the parent of NetNut Ltd., states in Exhibit 99.2, its press release of July 3, 2026, that on July 2, 2026 the company and NetNut 'became aware that certain domains associated with NetNut had been seized by the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigations (“FBI”)', that 'additional domains associated with NetNut have also been seized', and that 'the Company is currently experiencing disruptions to a portion of its services'. The exhibit gives no date for a return of the domains or of the service.

old: Three candidates for the 8 percent payload rate, tested rather than assumed. (1) The probe harness was at fault. Refuted for the payload measure: 8 of the same 100 lines carried a payload under the identical harness, and the failures split across five distinct error classes rather than one systematic failure, which is what per-host failure looks like and not what a broken client looks like. (2) The lines are stale, and the file is a large pool of long-dead addresses. Supported and not fully settled: 58 of 100 timed out and 19 failed at the socket, and the second run produced 15 handshakes against 17, so the population churns under the probe; but nothing here shows the file is unmaintained, only that most of its lines do not answer. (3) A vantage-point or diurnal effect on this machine. Not refuted, because two runs 23 minutes apart cannot separate it from a dead list, and only runs spread across a day could. The verdict rests on (2) with (3) open, and (3) does not change it: the payload rate would have to rise by an order of magnitude before the list became usable at a steady request volume. Weight: each rate is one sample of 100 lines drawn stratified across the three protocol files, taken twice, which is enough to show the yield is low and repeats and not enough to put an interval on it. A discrepancy between the assigned facts and the artefacts, recorded rather than smoothed. The facts give the working exits as OVH AS16276 twice, Contabo AS51167, DigitalOcean AS14061, Microsoft AS8075, GoDaddy AS26496 and AS398101, and Biznet AS17451. Re-deriving from the two named result files yields eight payload exits: OVH AS16276 twice, Biznet AS17451, Contabo AS51167, Microsoft AS8075 and GoDaddy AS26496, plus SCTS AS51004 and Liteserver AS60404, which are absent from the assigned list; DigitalOcean AS14061 and GoDaddy AS398101 appear in sources/p/72/72b4954ce06cf6a8b5e636d20b752d9169fd0f4389506c86f3d8506cacee7b33.json.gz against addresses that are not payload exits in either named file, so they belong to the wider lane-4 set rather than to this provider's eight. The datacenter conclusion survives the correction, since seven of the eight resolved to hosting ASNs and the eighth, SCTS, is a cable ISP; what changes is the roster, not the finding, and the verdict does not rest on it. On shape: the assignment names the interface tokens api, cli, rest, socks5, http-proxy, wireguard, openvpn, web-ui and none, but scripts/dossier/schema.json closes interface[] to its own enum, which has no proxy-protocol token, and scripts/dossier/validate.py enforces that enum; an in-memory test of socks5 and http-proxy against the schema returned two enum errors, so writing them would turn the gate red for the whole dossier tree. The array therefore carries rest, matching dossier/ip-proxy/proxyscrape-free-list.json, and the three protocols are stated in interface_detail. That gap is a defect worth naming: an ip-proxy topic cannot express what it is about until the enum gains socks5, http-proxy and a static-file token. Searched dossier/ and docs/ for an existing record naming TheSpeedX or PROXY-List to correct; the only hit is dossier/ip-proxy/proxyscrape-free-list.json and it is a substring match on free-proxy-list rather than a mention of this provider, so this record corrects nothing outside itself.
new: Run 1 dialled 100 lines drawn from the three files (40 HTTP, 40 SOCKS5, 20 SOCKS4): 17 completed a handshake and 8 carried a payload. The 92 lines without a payload split into five error classes: 58 TimeoutError, 19 OSError (7 of them an HTTP CONNECT answered with status 407), 7 ConnectionRefusedError, 5 body-not-json (an unrelated HTML page came back, such as a video recorder, a network camera or a login form) and 3 ConnectionResetError. Run 2 dialled the same 100 lines: 15 handshakes and 8 payloads, 6 of the payload lines common to both runs. The 8 run-1 payload exits map to AS16276 OVH (51.210.123.18 and 198.244.254.77), AS17451 Biznet, AS51004 Sakhalin Cable Telesystems, AS60404 Liteserver, AS51167 Contabo, AS8075 Microsoft and AS26496 GoDaddy. Four of the eight are SOCKS5 lines on 45.74.31.42 and 45.74.31.46 whose exit address differs from the line's address. The same lookup maps other addresses to AS14061 DigitalOcean and AS398101 GoDaddy; none of those addresses carried a payload in either run. A recheck of the 8 run-1 payload lines returned 4 payloads, with exits in ID, FR, GB and SG, and 4 timeouts.
